It was played by 14 teams. The national champion was [[Alianza Lima]], their first title in 19 years.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/peru97.html Rsssf.org Peru 1997][https://historialblanquiazul.com/temporada-1997/ Alianza Lima Temporada 1997][https://rpp.pe/futbol/descentralizado/alianza-lima-recordo-titulo-nacional-del-ano-1997-noticia-1444480 25 años después: Alianza Lima recordó título nacional del año 1997][https://depor.com/futbol-peruano/descentralizado/alianza-lima-dia-hoy-salio-campeon-luego-19-anos-mano-jorge-luis-pinto-1997-fotos-138351/ ¡Histórico! Un día como hoy Alianza Lima salió campeón luego de 19 años][https://libero.pe/futbol-peruano/1517307-inolvidable-alianza-lima-festejo-interminable-1997-video ¡Inolvidable! Alianza Lima y su festejo interminable en 1997] == Competition modus == The national championship was divided into two half-year [[tournament]]s, the [[Apertura 1997 (Peru)|Torneo Apertura]] and the [[Clausura 1997 (Peru)|Torneo Clausura]]. Each was played on a [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] basis. The winners of each would play for the national title in a playoff. However, since the same club won both tournaments, it won the national championship automatically. Following-season [[Copa Libertadores]] berths went to the champion, as well as to the winner of a Liguilla (''small league'') featuring teams between second and seventh place on the aggregate table. This had a round-robin format, with the team obtaining the best results in matchups during the "regular season" playing at home. The runner-up would qualify for the [[Copa CONMEBOL]].
